 10 Things To Know – South Carolina 
 Hunter Corneliusen 
 November 13, 2026 
 Arkansas returns inside the friendly confines of Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium to take on #20 South Carolina. Kickoff between the Hogs and Gamecocks, who were included in the College Football Playoff Selection Committee’s initial rankings, is set for 6:45 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 14, on SEC Network.
 1 – Saturday’s matchup will be the 25th meeting between the programs, with Arkansas leading the all-time series 14-10.  The Razorbacks earned a 44-30 win during the last matchup against the Gamecocks on Sept. 10, 2022 and have won four of the previous five meetings on The Hill dating back to 2007.
 2 – With 16 carries for 100 yards, RB Cam Settles recorded the first 100-yard rushing game of his collegiate career. He became the 10th Arkansas ball carrier in history to accomplish the feat against Auburn and registered the first 100-yard rushing performance by a Hog this season.
 3 – Arkansas holds a 9-7 all-time record in games played on Nov. 14.
 4 – The Razorbacks registered eight tackles for loss in last week’s contest at Auburn. It was the most tackles for loss since they registered eight during a 23-22 loss at LSU on Nov. 15, 2025.
 5 – Arkansas has scored in 67 consecutive games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in program history, and which is the fourth-longest streak in program history and longest since a 73-game streak from Sept. 30, 1961 to Nov. 25, 1972. Arkansas was last shut out on Oct. 2, 2021, in a loss to No. 2 Georgia.
 6 – The last time out at Auburn on Nov. 7, WR Chris Marshall led Arkansas in receptions (5) and receiving yards (65) for the seventh game this season. Marshall is the first Hog to lead Arkansas in receiving yards in 7+ games through nine games of a season since Marcus Monk (7) in 2006
 7 – The Arkansas defense has shut out opponents during the opening quarter in four games this season, accomplishing the feat against North Alabama, Tulsa, Tennessee and Auburn.
 8 – The Razorbacks’ 246 consecutive extra-points made streak, which began on Dec. 5, 2020, is the longest streak nationally by date.
 9 – RB Sutton Smith ’s 65-yard rush at the 12:20 mark in the second quarter of last week’s matchup at Auburn was the longest play from scrimmage by Arkansas this season and the longest rush since RB Rodney Hill’s 70-yard run during a 39-26 win over Texas Tech in the Liberty Bowl on Dec. 27, 2024. It was Smith’s second-longest run of his career, trailing only an 84-yard rush against East Carolina on Nov. 15, 2025, while at Memphis. It was also the longest rush by an opponent against Auburn since Texas A&M’s Amari Daniels’ 79-yard run on Sept. 23, 2023
 10 – With his 100-yard rushing performance at Auburn, RB Cam Settles joined RB Braylen Russell and RB T.J. Hammonds as Razorbacks who are Arkansas natives to have rushed for 100+ yards in a game this decade. Russell ran for 175 yards on 16 carries in a win over Mississippi State on Oct. 26, 2024, while Hammonds rushed for 119 yards and a touchdown on seven carries against Coastal Carolina on Nov. 4, 2017.
